items.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Special MCOCA court remands 11 accused to police custody till November 6
items.summary: Eleven persons, including two women, accused in the case registered after gun shots were fired towards Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Juhu have been remanded to police custody till November 6 by a special court designated to hear cases under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999 (MCOCA). Special Judge Satyanarayan Ramjivan Navandar passed the remand order on October 29. The Mumbai Police Crime Branch sought 10 days of custodial interrogation to probe a wider syndicate conspiracy. The invocation of MCOCA was sanctioned by the court on October 28 after the prosecution cited the criminal antecedents of six of the accused. The prosecution also cited financial motives, and an alleged bid to establish gang dominance. The Crime Branch informed the court that wanted operative Anil Pandit, suspected to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi syndicate and facing three chargesheets in Punjab and Haryana, had claimed responsibility for the assault through social media and audio messages. items.title: Byju's insolvency: Drama in Kerala High Court after judge flags out-of-turn listing; bench split on stay order
items.summary: Drama unfolded in court room 6D of the Kerala High Court on Thursday after a judge, sitting as part of a division bench, took exception to the out-of-turn listing of a case despite an earlier order stating that the matter was to be heard only on November 6. Justice Johnson John , the junior judge on the bench, said that the earlier order had clearly spelt out that the case was to be listed only on November 6 and that he was unaware as to why it came up for hearing today. “ I don’t want to explain further...I don’t know why it came up today. It was posted for November 6,” Justice John said. The case pertained to the ongoing insolvency proceedings against Think and Learn Private Limited, which owns edu-tech firm Byju’s. Listed before the Court was a review petition filed by Voizzit Technology (a creditor who has claimed right to the ownership of Byju’s) challenging the dismissal of a writ petition filed by it earlier seeking a probe into the insolvency proceedings.
